data.exact_reserve_text: The syndicate has continued to benefit from favourable development on the back years, contributing a saving of 6% on the loss ratio (2020 - 5%). During the 2021 calendar year we witnessed a further deterioration to the Golden Ray claim (a car carrier that capsized in September 2019 when leaving Brunswick Port in Georgia, USA). We also increased our reserves again for expected losses arising from the riots in Chile during late 2019. There was one noteworthy back year claim increase on the MSC Flaminia (2012 Year of Account).

prior_year_events.impact_description: further deterioration to the Golden Ray claim. The incurred claim to Syndicate 609 is now $13.0m gross and $8.6m net (falling on the Marine & Energy Liability, Cargo and Marine Reinsurance accounts).
increased our reserves again for expected losses arising from the riots in Chile during late 2019. They now stand at $11.0m and mostly impact the Non-Marine Property account.

one noteworthy back year claim increase on the MSC Flaminia (2012 Year of Account). This is a very complicated marine charterer's liability claim and following a recent court decision we re-established reserves.

named_events.loss_description: significant losses relating to COVID-19 (at 31 December 2021 - gross ultimate of $82.4m, and $76.5m net) the profitability of the syndicate has not been adversely affected. The ultimate claim has not moved materially during 2021 which is indicative of the stability of the initial reserve estimates. The remaining IBNR in relation to COVID-19 as at 31 December 2021 amounts to US$35.9m gross and US$30.4m net. The COVID-19 losses have contributed 1% to the net loss ratio (2020 - 10%) and has mainly affected the Accident and Health classes.

The largest was Hurricane Ida and at 31 December 2021 we estimate final claims from Ida to be $28.0m gross and $25.6m net. Of these, $18.1m fall on the 2021 Year of Account with the remainder falling back on to 2020 on a net basis. Lower severity catastrophe events such as Hurricane Ida and the Texas Winterstorms which have contributed 3% and 1% to the loss ratio respectively.

higher incidence of catastrophe losses in 2020 compared to 2021 primarily due to the COVID-19 and Hurricane Laura losses. Hurricane Laura was the largest natural catastrophe loss in 2020 and I am pleased to report that we have not seen any material movement on the expected ultimate claims during 2021.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall release of gross claims reserves of GBP 56.473 million in 2021, primarily driven by favorable development on back years. However, this was a mixed picture with specific strengthenings for prior year events such as the Golden Ray claim (2019), riots in Chile (late 2019), and the MSC Flaminia (2012) marine liability claim. The overall favorable development contributed to a saving on the loss ratio.
